Alopecia areata.fact: In patients with only one or two patches, this one-year recovery will occur in up to 80%.

Alopecia areata.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia areata.question: Among those in whom all body hair is lost, fewer than _____ recover
Alopecia areata.fact: Among those in whom all body hair is lost, fewer than 10% recover.

Alopecia areata.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia areata.question: About _____ of people are affected at any one time, and 2% of people are affected at some point in time
Alopecia areata.fact: About 0.15% of people are affected at any one time, and 2% of people are affected at some point in time.

Alopecia areata.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia areata.question: A 2020 systematic review showed greater than _____ hair regrowth in 80.9% of patients treated with 5 mg/mL triamcinolone injections
Alopecia areata.fact: A 2020 systematic review showed greater than 50% hair regrowth in 80.9% of patients treated with 5 mg/mL triamcinolone injections. A Cochrane-style systematic review published in 2019 showed 5% topical minoxidil was more than eight times more associated with >50% hair regrowth at 6 months compared to placebo.

Alopecia areata.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia areata.question: Studies indicate that people of Asian descent have the highest risk, with nearly _____ cases per 100 people, compared to fewer than 2 cases per 100 people among White individuals
Alopecia areata.fact: Studies indicate that people of Asian descent have the highest risk, with nearly 6 cases per 100 people, compared to fewer than 2 cases per 100 people among White individuals.

Alopecia areata.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia areata.question: The effects of the condition also differ by ethnicity: individuals of _____ descent with AA are more likely to experience anxiety and require medical leave from work
Alopecia areata.fact: The effects of the condition also differ by ethnicity: individuals of Black descent with AA are more likely to experience anxiety and require medical leave from work.

Alopecia areata.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia areata.question: "Areata" is derived from the _____ word, "area", meaning a vacant space or patch
Alopecia areata.fact: "Areata" is derived from the Latin word, "area", meaning a vacant space or patch.

Alopecia universalis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia universalis.question: The _____ was Loss of all body hair.
Alopecia universalis.fact: Alopecia universalis (AU), also called alopecia areata universalis, is a medical condition involving the loss of all body hair, including eyebrows, eyelashes, chest hair, armpit hair, and pubic hair.

Alopecia universalis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia universalis.question: In June _____, a 25-year-old man with almost no hair on his body was reported to have grown a full head of hair, as well as eyebrows, eyelashes, and facial, armpit, and other hair, following eight mon
Alopecia universalis.fact: In June 2014, a 25-year-old man with almost no hair on his body was reported to have grown a full head of hair, as well as eyebrows, eyelashes, and facial, armpit, and other hair, following eight months of treatment.

Alopecia universalis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia universalis.question: Genetic factors may contribute to AU, as about _____ of those affected have a family member with alopecia
Alopecia universalis.fact: Genetic factors may contribute to AU, as about 20% of those affected have a family member with alopecia.

Alopecia universalis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia universalis.question: A review that combined and analyzed the findings of 45 studies comprising 2,227 patients showed any hair regrowth in _____ and complete hair regrowth in 24.9% of patients with AT and AU using contact
Alopecia universalis.fact: A review that combined and analyzed the findings of 45 studies comprising 2,227 patients showed any hair regrowth in 54.5% and complete hair regrowth in 24.9% of patients with AT and AU using contact immunotherapy.

Alopecia universalis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Alopecia universalis.question: A controlled study comprising 28 patients found positive terminal hair growth in eight of the patients (_____) using a 0.05% clobetasol propionate ointment
Alopecia universalis.fact: A controlled study comprising 28 patients found positive terminal hair growth in eight of the patients (28.5%) using a 0.05% clobetasol propionate ointment.

Anagen effluvium.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anagen effluvium.question: The _____ was Pathologic loss of anagen or growth-phase hairs.
Anagen effluvium.fact: Anagen effluvium is the pathologic loss of anagen or growth-phase hairs. Anagen effluvium is due to an acute injury to the hair follicles by an endogenous or exogenous cause, resulting in sudden diffuse shedding of structurally damaged hairs.

Anagen effluvium.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anagen effluvium.question: Toxins that can interrupt hair growth include: _____ agents, usually prescribed to treat cancer, especially when multiple drugs are used or they are in high dose
Anagen effluvium.fact: Toxins that can interrupt hair growth include: Chemotherapy agents, usually prescribed to treat cancer, especially when multiple drugs are used or they are in high dose.

Anagen effluvium.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anagen effluvium.question: Other medicines such as colchicine and ciclosporin (ciclosporin more often causes increased hair growth) _____ such as thallium, arsenic, gold and bismuth
Anagen effluvium.fact: Other medicines such as colchicine and ciclosporin (ciclosporin more often causes increased hair growth) Poisons such as thallium, arsenic, gold and bismuth.

Anagen effluvium.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anagen effluvium.question: In anagen effluvium, histopathologic evaluation of a punch biopsy of the scalp will exhibit a normal anagen-to-telogen ratio, which is less than _____ telogen hair follicles
Anagen effluvium.fact: In anagen effluvium, histopathologic evaluation of a punch biopsy of the scalp will exhibit a normal anagen-to-telogen ratio, which is less than 15% telogen hair follicles. If greater than 15% of the hair follicles are in the telogen phase, this more supports a diagnosis of telogen effluvium.

Anagen effluvium.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anagen effluvium.question: If greater than _____ of the hair follicles are in the telogen phase, this more supports a diagnosis of telogen effluvium
Anagen effluvium.fact: In anagen effluvium, histopathologic evaluation of a punch biopsy of the scalp will exhibit a normal anagen-to-telogen ratio, which is less than 15% telogen hair follicles. If greater than 15% of the hair follicles are in the telogen phase, this more supports a diagnosis of telogen effluvium.

Andre Walker Hair Typing System.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.question: The _____ was Classification system for hair types.
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.fact: The Andre Walker Hair Typing System, also called The Hair Chart, is a classification system for hair types created in the 1990s by Oprah Winfrey's stylist Andre Walker.

Andre Walker Hair Typing System.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.question: The system has been criticized for an apparent hierarchy which values _____ hair over other hair types
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.fact: The system has been criticized for an apparent hierarchy which values Caucasian hair over other hair types.

Andre Walker Hair Typing System.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.question: In _____ the system was the subject of episodes of the podcasts 99% Invisible and The Stoop
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.fact: In 2018 the system was the subject of episodes of the podcasts 99% Invisible and The Stoop.

Andre Walker Hair Typing System.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.question: Research in the _____ of Women's Dermatology has suggested Walker's curl-classification system may be useful in conversations about alopecia and other health conditions
Andre Walker Hair Typing System.fact: Research in the International Journal of Women's Dermatology has suggested Walker's curl-classification system may be useful in conversations about alopecia and other health conditions.

Apocrine.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Apocrine.question: The _____ was Classification of secretion of exocrine glands.
Apocrine.fact: Apocrine () is a term used to classify the mode of secretion of exocrine glands. In apocrine secretion, secretory cells accumulate material at their apical ends, often forming blebs or "snouts", and this material then buds off from the cells, forming extracellular vesicles.

Apocrine.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Apocrine.question: The rate of incidence varies from 0.5 to _____
Apocrine.fact: The rate of incidence varies from 0.5 to 4%.

Birth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Birth.question: The _____ was Process of bearing offspring.
Birth.fact: Birth is the act or process of bearing or bringing forth offspring, also referred to in technical contexts as parturition. In some species, the offspring is precocial and can move around almost immediately after birth but in others, it is altricial and completely dependent on parenting.

Birth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Birth.question: In April _____, approximately 8-month old elephant twins were sighted joining their mother's herd in the Tarangire National Park of Tanzania, estimated to have been born in August 2017
Birth.fact: In April 2018, approximately 8-month old elephant twins were sighted joining their mother's herd in the Tarangire National Park of Tanzania, estimated to have been born in August 2017.

Birth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Birth.question: A fossil from Australia's _____, laid down in the Devonian period, 380 million years ago, was found with an embryo inside it connected by an umbilical cord to a yolk sac
Birth.fact: A fossil from Australia's Gogo Formation, laid down in the Devonian period, 380 million years ago, was found with an embryo inside it connected by an umbilical cord to a yolk sac.

Birth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Birth.question: Placoderms are a sister group of the ancestor of all living jawed fishes (_____), including both chondrichthyans, the sharks & rays, and Osteichthyes, the bony fishes
Birth.fact: Placoderms are a sister group of the ancestor of all living jawed fishes (Gnathostomata), including both chondrichthyans, the sharks & rays, and Osteichthyes, the bony fishes.

Birth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Birth.question: In a recently described example, an _____ species, Trachylepis ivensi, has developed a purely reptilian placenta directly comparable in structure and function to a mammalian placenta
Birth.fact: In a recently described example, an African species, Trachylepis ivensi, has developed a purely reptilian placenta directly comparable in structure and function to a mammalian placenta.

Body cavity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Body cavity.question: The _____ was Internal space within a multicellular organism.
Body cavity.fact: A body cavity is any space or compartment, or potential space, in an animal body. The two largest human body cavities are the ventral body cavity, and the dorsal body cavity.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: The _____ was Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
Defecation.fact: Defecation (or defaecation) follows digestion and is the necessary biological process by which organisms eliminate a solid, semisolid, or liquid waste material called feces (or faeces) from the digestive tract via the anus or cloaca.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: A _____-style flush toilet requires a sitting position, as compared with a squat toilet
Defecation.fact: A Western-style flush toilet requires a sitting position, as compared with a squat toilet.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: Squat toilets are used by the vast majority of the world, including most of Africa, Asia, and the _____
Defecation.fact: Squat toilets are used by the vast majority of the world, including most of Africa, Asia, and the Middle East.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: The use of sit-down toilets in the _____ world is a relatively recent development, beginning in the 19th century with the advent of indoor plumbing
Defecation.fact: The use of sit-down toilets in the Western world is a relatively recent development, beginning in the 19th century with the advent of indoor plumbing.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: Different levels of cumulative intestinal injuries can cause different complications, such as fistulae, damage of bowel function, symptom recurrence, _____, etc
Defecation.fact: Different levels of cumulative intestinal injuries can cause different complications, such as fistulae, damage of bowel function, symptom recurrence, disability, etc.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: Ulcerative colitis mainly affects the function of the large bowel, and its incidence rate is three times greater than that of _____'s disease
Defecation.fact: Ulcerative colitis mainly affects the function of the large bowel, and its incidence rate is three times greater than that of Crohn's disease.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: Cardiac arrest and other cardiovascular complications can in rare cases occur due to attempting to defecate using the _____ maneuver
Defecation.fact: Cardiac arrest and other cardiovascular complications can in rare cases occur due to attempting to defecate using the Valsalva maneuver. Valsalva retinopathy is another pathological syndrome associated with the Valsalva maneuver.

Defecation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Defecation.question: Also, in releasing the _____ maneuver blood pressure falls; this, coupled with standing up quickly to leave the toilet, can result in a blackout
Defecation.fact: Valsalva retinopathy is another pathological syndrome associated with the Valsalva maneuver. Also, in releasing the Valsalva maneuver blood pressure falls; this, coupled with standing up quickly to leave the toilet, can result in a blackout.

Drinking.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Drinking.question: The _____ was Ingestion of water or other liquids.
Drinking.fact: Drinking is the act of ingesting water or other liquids into the body through the mouth, proboscis, or elsewhere. The physiological processes of drinking vary widely among other animals.

Drinking.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Drinking.question: Some desert insects, such as _____ unguicularis, have evolved to drink substantially from nighttime fog
Drinking.fact: Some desert insects, such as Onymacris unguicularis, have evolved to drink substantially from nighttime fog.

Drinking.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Drinking.question: Evidence of fermented drinks in human culture goes back as early as the _____, and the first pictorial evidence can be found in Egypt around 4,000 BC
Drinking.fact: Evidence of fermented drinks in human culture goes back as early as the Neolithic Period, and the first pictorial evidence can be found in Egypt around 4,000 BC.

Ear canal.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ear canal.question: The _____ was Tube running from the outer ear to the middle ear.
Ear canal.fact: The ear canal (external acoustic meatus, external auditory meatus, EAM) is a pathway running from the outer ear to the middle ear. The adult human ear canal extends from the auricle to the eardrum and is about 25 millimetres (1 in) in length and 7 millimetres (0.3 in) in diameter.

Eating.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Eating.question: The _____ was Ingestion of food.
Eating.fact: Eating (also called feeding or consuming) is the ingestion of food for digestion. Animals, in particular, have evolved different forms of eating — carnivores and scavengers eat flesh (meat) from other animals, herbivores and algivores eat plants and algae, omnivores consume a mixture of both plant and animal matters, and detritivores and coprophages eat detritus and feces.

Eating.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Eating.question: The first one is cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript (_____), the second is α-MSH (α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone)
Eating.fact: The first one is cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript (CART), the second is α-MSH (α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone).

Eating.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Eating.question: These include depression, food allergies, ingestion of certain chemicals, bulimia, anorexia nervosa, pituitary gland malfunction and other endocrine problems, and _____er illnesses and eating disorders
Eating.fact: These include depression, food allergies, ingestion of certain chemicals, bulimia, anorexia nervosa, pituitary gland malfunction and other endocrine problems, and numerous other illnesses and eating disorders.

Ejaculation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculation.question: The _____ was Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
Ejaculation.fact: Ejaculation is the discharge of semen (the ejaculate; normally containing sperm) from the penis through the urethra. Ejaculation involves involuntary contractions of the pelvic floor and is normally linked with orgasm.

Ejaculation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculation.question: A summary of semen development is shown in _____ 1
Ejaculation.fact: A summary of semen development is shown in Table 1.

Ejaculation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculation.question: ^a_____ is jellylike and fails to liquefy
Ejaculation.fact: ^aEjaculate is jellylike and fails to liquefy. ^cEjaculate liquefies within an hour.

Ejaculation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculation.question: ^c_____ liquefies within an hour
Ejaculation.fact: ^aEjaculate is jellylike and fails to liquefy. ^cEjaculate liquefies within an hour.

Ejaculation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculation.question: Some doctors speculate that the frequency of _____ "in the population may be greater than has been reported in the academic literature", and that many POIS sufferers are undiagnosed
Ejaculation.fact: A small fraction of men have a disease called postorgasmic illness syndrome (POIS), which causes severe muscle pain throughout the body and other symptoms immediately following ejaculation. Some doctors speculate that the frequency of POIS "in the population may be greater than has been reported in the academic literature", and that many POIS sufferers are undiagnosed.

Ejaculation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ejaculation.question: The first report and footage of spontaneous ejaculation in an aquatic mammal was recorded in a wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin near Mikura Island, Japan, in _____
Ejaculation.fact: The first report and footage of spontaneous ejaculation in an aquatic mammal was recorded in a wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin near Mikura Island, Japan, in 2012.

Heart valve.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Heart valve.question: The _____ was Flap of tissue that prevent backflow of blood around the heart.
Heart valve.fact: A heart valve (cardiac valve) is a biological one-way valve that allows blood to flow in one direction through the chambers of the heart. Heart valves are opened or closed by a difference in blood pressure on each side.

Heart valve.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Heart valve.question: These relationships are based on the _____ equations
Heart valve.fact: These relationships are based on the Euler equations.

Heart valve.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Heart valve.question: Less common CHD's are tricuspid and pulmonary atresia, and _____'s anomaly
Heart valve.fact: Less common CHD's are tricuspid and pulmonary atresia, and Ebstein's anomaly. Ebstein's anomaly is the displacement of the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve causing a larger atrium and a smaller ventricle than normal.

Heart valve.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Heart valve.question: The valve was first implanted in a patient in _____ and remained in use, globally, until it was replaced in 2007 by Edwards' company, Edwards Lifesciences, with a new ring design
Heart valve.fact: The valve was first implanted in a patient in 1960 and remained in use, globally, until it was replaced in 2007 by Edwards' company, Edwards Lifesciences, with a new ring design.

Internal urethral orifice.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Internal urethral orifice.question: The _____ was Opening of the urinary bladder.
Internal urethral orifice.fact: The internal urethral orifice is the opening of the urinary bladder into the urethra.

Lacrimal sac.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Lacrimal sac.question: The _____ was Upper, dilated end of the nasolacrimal duct.
Lacrimal sac.fact: The lacrimal sac or lachrymal sac is the upper dilated end of the nasolacrimal duct, and is lodged in a deep groove formed by the lacrimal bone and frontal process of the maxilla. Lacrimal sac occlusion leads to dacryocystitis.

Menstruation (mammal).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Menstruation (mammal).question: The _____ was Periodic shedding of the uterine lining.
Menstruation (mammal).fact: Menstruation is the shedding of the uterine lining (endometrium) in some mammals. It occurs on a regular basis in uninseminated sexually reproductive-age females of certain mammal species.

Menstruation (mammal).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Menstruation (mammal).question: It is common in simians (_____ monkeys, New World monkeys, and apes), but completely lacking in strepsirrhine primates and possibly weakly present in tarsiers
Menstruation (mammal).fact: It is common in simians (Old World monkeys, New World monkeys, and apes), but completely lacking in strepsirrhine primates and possibly weakly present in tarsiers.

Menstruation (mammal).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Menstruation (mammal).question: Beyond primates, it is known only in bats, the elephant shrew, and the spiny mouse species _____ cahirinus
Menstruation (mammal).fact: Beyond primates, it is known only in bats, the elephant shrew, and the spiny mouse species Acomys cahirinus.

Mouth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Mouth.question: The _____ was First portion of the alimentary canal that receives food.
Mouth.fact: A mouth, also called the oral, is the body orifice through which many animals ingest food and vocalize. The body cavity immediately behind the mouth opening, called the oral cavity (or cavum oris in Latin), is also the first part of the alimentary canal, which leads to the pharynx and the gullet.

Mouth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Mouth.question: Most bilaterian phyla, including arthropods, molluscs and _____, have a two-opening gut tube with a mouth at one end and an anus at the other
Mouth.fact: Most bilaterian phyla, including arthropods, molluscs and chordates, have a two-opening gut tube with a mouth at one end and an anus at the other.

Mouth.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Mouth.question: Sea urchins have a set of five sharp calcareous plates, which are used as jaws and are known as _____'s lantern
Mouth.fact: Sea urchins have a set of five sharp calcareous plates, which are used as jaws and are called Aristotle's lantern.

ADME.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
ADME.question: The _____ was Acronym for process of disposition of pharmaceutical compounds.
ADME.fact: ADME is the four-letter abbreviation (acronym) for absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion, and is mainly used in fields such as pharmacokinetics and pharmacology. The term ADME was first introduced in the 1960s, and has become a standard term widely used in scientific literature, teaching, drug regulations, and clinical practice.

ADME.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
ADME.question: Excretion of drugs by the kidney involves 3 main mechanisms: _____ filtration of unbound drug
ADME.fact: Excretion of drugs by the kidney involves 3 main mechanisms: Glomerular filtration of unbound drug.

Agonist-antagonist.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Agonist-antagonist.question: A _____ agonist can produce the largest response that the tissue is capable of giving
Agonist-antagonist.fact: Which is a substance that fully activates and causes resultant cellular changes in the receptor that it binds to while producing an effect within the cell. A Full agonist can produce the largest response that the tissue is capable of giving.

Bacteriostatic agent.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bacteriostatic agent.question: The _____ was Agent that stops bacteria from reproducing.
Bacteriostatic agent.fact: A bacteriostatic agent or bacteriostat, abbreviated Bstatic, is a biological or chemical agent that stops bacteria from reproducing, while not necessarily killing them otherwise.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: The _____ was In biochemistry, the preference of ligands to bind with one receptor over another.
Binding selectivity.fact: In chemistry, binding selectivity is defined with respect to the binding of ligands to a substrate forming a complex. Binding selectivity describes how a ligand may bind more preferentially to one receptor than another.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: The specificity of a receptor is determined by its spatial geometry and the way it binds to the ligand through non-covalent interactions, such as hydrogen bonding or Van der _____ forces
Binding selectivity.fact: The specificity of a receptor is determined by its spatial geometry and the way it binds to the ligand through non-covalent interactions, such as hydrogen bonding or Van der Waals forces.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: The further use of quantitative structure-activity relationships (_____) led to the development of other agents such as ranitidine
Binding selectivity.fact: The further use of quantitative structure-activity relationships (QSAR) led to the development of other agents such as ranitidine.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: When the metal exists as a divalent ion, such as with lead, Pb2+ or mercury, Hg2+ selectivity against calcium, Ca2+ and magnesium, _____, is essential in order that the treatment does not remove essential metals
Binding selectivity.fact: When the metal exists as a divalent ion, such as with lead, Pb2+ or mercury, Hg2+ selectivity against calcium, Ca2+ and magnesium, Mg2+, is essential in order that the treatment does not remove essential metals.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: deferoxamine, a naturally occurring siderophore produced by the actinobacter _____ pilosus and was used initially as a chelation therapy agent
Binding selectivity.fact: deferoxamine, a naturally occurring siderophore produced by the actinobacter Streptomyces pilosus and was used initially as a chelation therapy agent.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: This ion is classified as borderline in the scheme of _____, Chatt and Davies
Binding selectivity.fact: This ion is classified as borderline in the scheme of Ahrland, Chatt and Davies.

Binding selectivity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Binding selectivity.question: For example, _____ may be administered as a calcium salt to reduce the removal of calcium from bone together with the heavy metal
Binding selectivity.fact: For example, EDTA may be administered as a calcium salt to reduce the removal of calcium from bone together with the heavy metal.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: The _____ was Similarity between preparations of a drug.
Bioequivalence.fact: Bioequivalence is a term in pharmacokinetics used to assess the expected in vivo biological equivalence of two proprietary preparations of a drug. One article defined bioequivalence by stating that, "two pharmaceutical products are bioequivalent if they are pharmaceutically equivalent and their bioavailabilities (rate and extent of availability) after administration in the same molar dose are similar to such a degree that their effects, with respect to both efficacy and safety, can be expecte...

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: For high variable finished pharmaceutical products, the applicable acceptance range for _____ can be expanded (up to 69.84–143.19%)
Bioequivalence.fact: For a pharmacokinetic comparison, the plasma concentration data are used to assess key pharmacokinetic parameters such as area under the curve (AUC), peak concentration (Cmax), time to peak concentration (tmax), and absorption lag time (tlag). For high variable finished pharmaceutical products, the applicable acceptance range for Cmax can be expanded (up to 69.84–143.19%).

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: There are tighter requirements for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index and/or saturable metabolism – thus no generic products exist on the _____ market for digoxin or phenytoin for instance
Bioequivalence.fact: There are tighter requirements for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index and/or saturable metabolism – thus no generic products exist on the Australian market for digoxin or phenytoin for instance.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: This is considered demonstrated if the 90% confidence intervals (90% CI) of the ratios for AUC0–t and _____ between the two preparations lie in the range 80–125%
Bioequivalence.fact: For high variable finished pharmaceutical products, the applicable acceptance range for Cmax can be expanded (up to 69.84–143.19%). This is considered demonstrated if the 90% confidence intervals (90% CI) of the ratios for AUC0–t and Cmax between the two preparations lie in the range 80–125%.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: Since _____, National Centralized Volume-Based Procurement uses "passes generic-consistency evalulation" as one of the bidding criteria
Bioequivalence.fact: Since 2019, National Centralized Volume-Based Procurement uses "passes generic-consistency evalulation" as one of the bidding criteria.

Bioequivalence.fact: The Chinese definition of "bioequivalence" entails having the test drug's geometric mean Cmax, AUC(0–t), and AUC(0–∞) fall into 80%–125% of the reference drug in both fasting and fed states. If pharmacokinetic values such as Cmax do not apply to the type of drug (e.g.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: (_____), the Consistency Evaluation Policy increased R&D spending for Chinese pharmaceutical companies, especially among private and high-yielding ones
Bioequivalence.fact: (2022), the Consistency Evaluation Policy increased R&D spending for Chinese pharmaceutical companies, especially among private and high-yielding ones.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: (_____) argues that the Policy increased the innovation quality of the Chinese pharmaceutical industry
Bioequivalence.fact: (2023) argues that the Policy increased the innovation quality of the Chinese pharmaceutical industry.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: In _____, two providers of consumer information on nutritional products and supplements, ConsumerLab.com and The People's Pharmacy, released the results of comparative tests of different brands of bup
Bioequivalence.fact: In 2007, two providers of consumer information on nutritional products and supplements, ConsumerLab.com and The People's Pharmacy, released the results of comparative tests of different brands of bupropion.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: The tests showed that some generic versions of _____ 300 mg didn't perform the same as the brand-name pill in laboratory tests
Bioequivalence.fact: The tests showed that some generic versions of Wellbutrin XL 300 mg didn't perform the same as the brand-name pill in laboratory tests. The FDA investigated these complaints and concluded that the generic version is equivalent to Wellbutrin XL in regard to bioavailability of bupropion and its main active metabolite hydroxybupropion.

Bioequivalence.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bioequivalence.question: The FDA investigated these complaints and concluded that the generic version is equivalent to _____ XL in regard to bioavailability of bupropion and its main active metabolite hydroxybupropion
